newsitem.title: GHANA: SOCCER-GHANA DROP YEBOAH FOR CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GHANA DROP YEBOAH FOR CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: Ghana striker Tony Yeboah has been punished for bad behaviour and dropped for his country's World Cup qualifier against Gabon on Sunday.
Yeboah, who plays with English premier league club Leeds, clashed with Ghana's deputy coach Sam Arday after being substituted in a qualifier against Sierra Leone two weeks ago.
He has been replaced in the side by Luton Town's Kim Grant.
"(Yeboah's) behaviour cannot be tolerated," Dutch coach Israel Rinus said. "When I am in charge it is impossible to accept such things.
The Ghanaian landed in hot water after a similar incident at his English club last month.
He was fined two weeks' pay for ripping off his Leeds shirt and throwing it at manager George Graham after being substituted in a league match.
Yeboah, who joined Leeds from Germany's Eintracht Frankfurt for 3.4 million pounds ($5.4 million), was sidelined for two months late last year after a cartilage operation.

"I was satisfied by Yeboah's form in the first 70 minutes of the game," said Rinus, adding that Arday had no hand in the substitution decision. "I realised that (Yeboah) was not fit to play for the full 90 minutes."
Israel was appointed national coach last month.

Ghana's chances received a boost following Munich 1860's decision to release captain Abedi Pele for the vital qualifying match. Ghana's Football Association had threatened the German club with FIFA sanctions.
Ghana must beat Gabon to keep alive their slim hopes of qualifying for next year's finals in France.
